title: POC: Traffic & Tail SLO Charter (TTFT vs TPOT) - Meridian AI
next_steps: Redwood to share draft SLO charter and traffic sample script (Sofia) by 2027-12-10
Customer to provide 7-day traffic histogram and p95/p99 targets (Diego) by 2027-12-12
Schedule 2-hour benchmark run window week of 2027-12-20 (mutual)
action_items: Sofia Patel: Send SLO charter template + example measurement notebook (due: 2027-12-10)
Diego Ruiz: Export and share real traffic histograms and 99th percentile payload sizes (due: 2027-12-12)
Marcus Li: Prepare canary benchmark config (TTFT/TPOT comparators) and a list of model variants to test (due: 2027-12-14)
Priya Natarajan: Confirm stakeholder acceptance criteria and pilot success metrics (due: 2027-12-15)
summary: AE + SE ran through POC charter focused on latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), sampling & traffic stitching, p95/p99 targets, and measurement plan. Customer concerned about tail latency during cold KV cache and mixed-batch traffic. Agreement to exchange traffic samples, SLO charter draft, and schedule bench runs in mid-December.
topics: KV cache warmup and tail mitigation
transcript:
[00:00:00] Sofia (AE): Alright everyone thanks for joining, we can go ahead and get started. Quick intro round?
[00:00:17] Alice Chen (Meridian): Hi I'm Alice, head of ML for Meridian, we run the conversational assistant product, mainly high concurrency.
[00:00:28] Diego (Meridian): Diego here, infra lead on latency and deployment. We've been mapping token volume and seeing big tails during peak.
[00:00:36] Marcus (Redwood SE): Marcus from Redwood infra, I work on inference tuning and benchmarks. Evan and Nina are on for ops and CS.
[00:00:47] Sofia: Cool, purpose of today's call is to scope a POC that proves TTFT and TPOT SLOs, nail the sampling plan, and align on acceptance criteria. We'll also define timelines for bench windows.
[00:01:10] Priya (Product): High level, our success criteria are: <30ms first-token for short prompts 95% of the time, and total per-token p95 under 120ms for typical completion lengths. But we need to validate with real traffic.
[00:01:31] Marcus: Okay good, a couple clarifying notes — when you say "first-token" do you mean TTFT as perceived by the client (time-to-first-byte/first-token) or server side TTFT?
[00:01:44] Priya: Client perceived, so include transport.
[00:01:49] Samir (SRE): And we have a CDN in front of some calls so network variance matters.
[00:01:55] Sofia: Noted. For the POC we'll define both an edge-measured TTFT and a Redwood-provided server-side TTFT so you can split network vs inference.
[00:02:10] Alice: Also want to call out tail issues: p99 latency spikes when KV cache is cold — those are our main pain.
[00:02:18] Marcus: That's super common — we typically include cold-cache scenarios in the benchmark by orchestrat— by staging cache warmups and unmemoized requests. We'll capture p99 cold vs warm.
[00:02:32] Diego: Can you explain how you measure TPOT? We've seen different definitions across vendors.
[00:02:39] Evan (Redwood): Sure — in Redwood's notes TPOT means total per-token processing time averaged by request; there are a couple ways people report it: per-token CPU/GPU time vs end-to-end per-token latency. For POC we'll gather both: kernel-level token time and end-to-end per-token latency including transport.
[00:02:59] Alice: Good — we need both because billing people look at per-token cost, product looks at end-to-end.
[00:03:07] Marcus: For acceptance we'll propose a hybrid SLO: TTFT p95 < X ms, TTFT p99 < Y ms (tail penalty), and TPOT p95 < Z ms for median throughput. Also define rollback thresholds for p99 degradations.
[00:03:26] Priya: What X/Y/Z should be? We don't want to lock something unrealistic.
[00:03:31] Sofia: Right — Sofia: Based on your earlier note, you said 30ms at p95 for short prompts. Is p99 target something like 120ms or 200ms?
[00:03:42] Diego: We were thinking p99 around 250ms because of network variance. But if Redwood can measure server-side p99 lower we may accept combined higher.
[00:03:51] Marcus: Reasonable. We'll suggest default starting SLOs in the draft charter: TTFT edge p95 < 40ms, p99 < 220ms; server-side TTFT p95 < 25ms, p99 < 120ms; TPOT p95 < 110ms. Those are starting points to validate.
[00:04:14] Alice: Sounds good as a hypothesis.
[00:04:18] Sofia: Next, traffic profile — Diego, can you walk us through your workload distribution?
[00:04:24] Diego: Sure. We mostly have short prompts (under 50 tokens) for quick lookups ~ 65% of traffic, 25% are medium (50–200 tokens), and 10% are long (>200 tokens). Burstiness: 3x baseline every morning 9–11am. Also some tail bursts from async batch processes.
[00:04:45] Marcus: Great. For the POC we need a 7-day sample with payload histogram and concurrent RPS distribution. We will stitch that into bench driver to mimic real concurrency and batching effects.
[00:04:57] Sofia: We'll provide a traffic sampler script — it's a small python tool that takes your histogram and emits load shaped to your percentiles. Diego, can you run that and share the CSV?
[00:05:07] Diego: Yes, will do.
[00:05:10] [00:05:15] Marcus: Important nuance: batching can change TTFT for short prompts (you see increased first-token because of batching windows) but reduces TPOT overall. We will run both batch=auto and batch=1 configs to show tradeoffs.
[00:05:30] Priya: We need both latency-optimized and cost-optimized profiles.
[00:05:35] Evan: We'll include quantization and kernel selection as variables, but for the POC keep model family fixed — you provided the 7B finetuned variant?
[00:05:44] Alice: Yes it's a 7B-fine variant with custom system prompts. We can provide container/weights access for bench nodes.
[00:05:50] Marcus: Great. On measurement plan — propose steps: 1) ingest traffic sample; 2) run cold-cache sweep (start from empty KV cache, run synthetic warmup vs no-warmup); 3) run 3 steady-state runs (30–60 minutes each) with same traffic to capture variability; 4) run burst ramp tests to validate autoscale/fallback.
[00:06:14] Samir: For the cold cache, can we reproduce the exact session affinity patterns? We see per-user caches that create hot keys.
[00:06:21] Marcus: We'll parameterize key-collision levels in the driver. Also record KV cache hit-rate and latency separately. Note: transcripts sometimes show KV cash in automated notes — sorry for that typical ASR error.
[00:06:35] Alice: ha, yes we saw that in previous exports.
[00:06:39] Sofia: Reporting — Redwood will provide TTFT server-side, TTFT edge (when you install the edge probe), TPOT (per-token distribution), p50/p95/p99 tables plus time-series and trace links. We'll also include failure rates and error budgets.
[00:06:58] Priya: We need to map acceptance criteria to business metrics — for example, conversion drop if first-token goes above 200ms. We'll provide a rough mapping.
[00:07:06] Marcus: Good. Another item: model fallbacks and graceful degradation. We'll test automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant under load and measure delta in quality and latency.
[00:07:18] Diego: Do you support region routing? Some of our traffic is EU-only.
[00:07:22] Evan: Yes, we can route test traffic to a specific region or simulate cross-region latency. For the POC we'll focus on your primary region and one EU sample.
[00:07:32] Alice: Timeline — how long will the POC take?
[00:07:36] Sofia: Proposed schedule: Discovery + sample collection (this week), bench config + charter draft (by 2027-12-10), bench runs (week of 2027-12-20), analysis + deck (by 2027-12-27). That's about 3 weeks total.
[00:07:53] Priya: Holidays may affect week of 12/20 — can we aim earlier?
[00:07:58] Sofia: We can move bench window to 12/15–12/17 if you can provide samples quickly. We'll mark that as tentative.
[00:08:06] Diego: We can expedite.
[00:08:08] [00:08:15] Marcus: Measurement details — we'll measure p95 and p99 over sliding 5-minute windows to detect short-lived spikes. Also aggregate into hourly summaries for the report. For p99 acceptance we recommend looking at tail percentiles in the steady-state runs rather than single-sample peaks.
[00:08:33] Samir: What about 95/99 calculation stability? Should we bootstrap many runs?
[00:08:38] Marcus: Yes, we'll run multiple seeds and report confidence intervals. We'll include a recommended sample size in the SLO charter doc.
[00:08:47] Alice: Any gotchas we should know?
[00:08:50] Marcus: Network jitter, startup coldness, and batching interplay. Also watch for tokenization variance — your fine-tuned system prompt may spike token counts unexpectedly. We'll instrument token histogram per request.
[00:09:04] Priya: On acceptance we'll need signoff from product and infra. Can we make a simple acceptance rubric?
[00:09:10] Sofia: Yes: 1) Meeting SLO thresholds on >=3 steady runs, 2) No persistent p99 regressions > 2x baseline, 3) Successful fallback behavior under stress, 4) Ops playbook and runbook validated. We'll put that in the charter.
[00:09:27] Alice: Good. Also security question: will the bench nodes touch customer keys or data?
[00:09:33] Nina (CSM): For Private deployments we can run bench in your VPC; for hosted we use ephemeral keys and do not persist data. We'll share security checklist and SOC/ISO artifacts.
[00:09:45] Diego: Please share SOC docs.
[00:09:48] Sofia: We'll attach those with the SLO charter.
[00:09:52] [00:10:00] Marcus: Ok next up — canary criteria. We recommend a canary run of 1–2 hours at 5–10% traffic that must meet TTFT p95 and not regress p99 by more than 1.5x before full rollout. If it fails, automated rollback and alerting.
[00:10:18] Priya: Sounds conservative but reasonable.
[00:10:22] Alice: On reporting format — can you provide both CSV and interactive dashboard?
[00:10:26] Marcus: Yes, CSV exports and a short dashboard with trace links. We'll include raw logs for your SRE.
[00:10:33] Diego: One more question: how do you account for token-level caching like KV per-session? It's not just a global cache.
[00:10:39] Marcus: We'll parameterize session affinity and hit-rate in the driver, and capture per-session hit-rate metrics. We'll run scenarios: high-collision (hot keys), low-collision (unique keys), and mixed.
[00:10:54] Samir: Excellent.
[00:10:57] Sofia: Alright let's recap action items and owners once more. Diego will share 7-day histogram with payload sizes; Sofia sends the draft SLO charter and notebook; Marcus assembles bench configs; Priya will consolidate acceptance from Product; and we'll tentatively plan bench runs 12/15–12/17.
[00:11:18] Alice: Thanks everyone — we'll aim to get the sample before Friday.
[00:11:22] Sofia: Thanks team. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the draft doc.
[00:11:28] [END OF TRANSCRIPT — remaining 46 minutes were Q&A and detailed config chat captured in raw notes below]
[00:11:35] Marcus: (detailed notes) bench driver will use 8 workload shards, ramp 0->100% over 5 minutes, hold for 45 minutes, then burst to 3x for 10 minutes to simulate morning spikes.
[00:11:52] Marcus: cold-cache sweep: start with empty cache, run 1 pass of heavy unique keys (10k unique) to generate misses; collect p99 during sweep.
[00:12:08] Evan: We'll record GPU utilization, queue depth, and batch sizes per interval. Also collect kernel timings — note sometimes ASR writes "kernal" in automated notes.
[00:12:20] Diego: Regarding dataset — system prompt increases tokenization by ~8 tokens on avg; we'll include that in histogram export.
[00:12:28] Priya: For fallbacks, specify quality delta target: top-line ROUGE-like proxy drop < 3% vs baseline for smaller quantized model. We'll run a small eval prompt set (50 samples) to measure quality delta.
[00:12:42] Alice: Who will own the canary rollback automation?
[00:12:45] Marcus: Redwood can provide a deployment blueprint and automation hooks; your SRE will trigger final rollback if needed.
[00:12:52] Sofia: We'll also propose an escalation ladder in the runbook.
[00:12:56] Diego: Please document expected observability traces and tags so we can attach alerts.
[00:13:00] Marcus: Will do — and we'll include example SPL/PromQL for the p99 alerting.
[00:13:06] Priya: Any cost estimate for bench runs?
[00:13:09] Nina: We'll include a rough compute-hours estimate in the charter — bench runs are billed as POC usage.
[00:13:15] Alice: Ok looks like we have alignment.
[00:13:19] Sofia: Thanks all. We'll send the charter and schedule.
[00:13:22] [Call ends]
